https://www.romania-insider.com/tarom-ce.text: Transport Romanian government replaces Tarom CEO on alleged unrealistic budget 23 July 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn The interim minister of transport, Radu Miruta, announced that the Board of Directors at flag carrier Tarom replaced interim CEO Bogdan Costas with Cristian Anghel, accusing the company’s management of failure to amend the 2026 budget plan that both sides agree is no longer realistic and revise the restructuring plan in line with market developments. The Transport Ministry, as the sole owner of Tarom, has not approved the company’s budget of revenues and expenditures for the current year. “They came up with a ridiculously unrealistic budget. We asked and demanded that it be restored to real figures. They didn't restore it. Maybe because there was no room left for fancy plans using public money,” minister Miruta explained. Tarom needs to break even by the end of the year, under the restructuring plan linked to the state aid extended by the government. Radu Miruta claimed that the dismissed CEO did not take any steps to restore the budget based on real data and delayed the steps to modify the restructuring plan. “The board of directors found today that the director did not take any steps to restore the budget based on real data and unreasonably delayed the steps to the European Commission to modify the restructuring plan, in accordance with market reality. [...]For months, the company's executive management, appointed by PSD, has been asking me to approve, as a shareholder, a budget built on figures that it itself knows are unrealistic,” minister Miruta said. The outgoing CEO claimed that the company took formal steps to amend the restructuring plan. "In May 2026: I officially opened technical discussions with representatives of the European Commission. In May 2026: I submitted to the Board of Directors a formal proposal containing the 4 strategic coordinates on which action was needed to adjust the plan. In May 2026: I obtained the Favorable Opinion of the Board of Directors for this adjustment strategy. All these documents were officially sent to the Ministry of Transport and minister Radu Miruţă. The ministry's response was total blockage: a complete lack of reaction. The minister did not approve the clear steps for adjustment, preferring later to blame the executive leadership," outgoing CEO Bogdan Costat claimed, as reported by Ziarul Financiar . iulian@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Johnypan/Dreamstime.com ) Normal Transport Romanian government replaces Tarom CEO on alleged unrealistic budget 23 July 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? https://fox11online.com/news/local/apple.text: APPLETON (WLUK) -- The City of Appleton is honoring one of its most famous residents, Harry Houdini. Oct. 31 will mark the 100th anniversary of the late magician's death. To commemorate the event, Appleton has a special celebration planned at Houdini Plaza on Halloween which will soon feature a new addition in his honor. "We applied to the state to be able to host a Harry Houdini Wisconsin historical marker right here in Houdini Plaza," Appleton Downtown Inc. Executive Director Jennifer Stephany said. Stephany said her organization worked closely with the Wisconsin Historical Society to get the new plaque. It's meant to recognize Houdini and the impact he had on Wisconsin's history. Houdini was born in Hungary, but his family moved to Appleton in 1878 when he was just four years old. He went on to become the well-known magician and escape artist we remember today. "You think about the history and the mark that he made on the art and industry of magic, and it's really unmatched. And it's really an honor for the community of Appleton and the Fox Cities to be able to honor that legacy right here in downtown Appleton," Stephany said. The marker will even note Houdini once performed at the Appleton Opera House. Houdini Plaza already has several tributes to the magician, but Stephany hopes the new marker will remind people of Houdini’s lasting impact on Appleton. "We're proud to be able to have this in our community for years and years to come," she said. The full inscription of what the historical marker will read as provided by the Wisconsin Historical Society: Harry Houdini was a world-famous magician and escape artist. Born Ehrich Weiss in Budapest, Hungary, he immigrated to the United States with his family when he was four years old, settling in Appleton in a home near this site in 1878. Houdini’s father, Mayer Samuel Weiss, was the first rabbi of Appleton’s Zion Reform Jewish Congregation. Throughout his career, Houdini claimed Appleton as his hometown. In 1897, he and his wife, Bess, performed at the Appleton Opera House. He even challenged the local police, escaping from handcuffs and a jail cell. Houdini traveled to Europe in 1900, where his performances brought him international recognition. Houdini was also an author, aviator, silent film star, inventor, and collector. He died at age 52 in 1926. Appleton proudly remembers its connection to the legendary “Handcuff King.”
